title: PurpleForge lab-spec
description: Declarative specification for a Purple-Team-instrumented Active Directory lab. Validated and reconciled by the lab-spec skill before any Terraform/Ansible is generated.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability ids from catalog/vulnerabilities/*.yml — the intentional gaps.

on_conflict.description: How to resolve a hardening control that would neutralize a selected vulnerability (see catalog vuln 'neutralized_by').

name.description: Lab identifier. Used as resource-name prefix, so it must be safe for cloud resource naming.

isolation.description: Access model for the lab network. Only vpn-only is supported: no vulnerable host may carry a public IP or accept inbound RDP/WinRM from the internet.

auto_shutdown.description: Local time + IANA timezone at which the lab is auto-stopped, e.g. '20:00 Europe/Madrid'.

budget_alert_usd.description: Cloud budget alert threshold in USD. Required so cost is tracked as code.

bastion_size.description: Cloud VM size for the WireGuard bastion, overriding the default (Azure: 'Standard_B1s'). Set it when the subscription's regional vCPU quota restricts the B-series (the #1 deploy blocker) — no need to touch templates. When absent, forge's default applies.

netbios.description: NetBIOS domain name (max 15 chars, AD constraint).

target.description: domain of another entry in forest[] this domain trusts.

services.description: Only meaningful on member-server; enables prerequisites for some catalog vulnerabilities (e.g. adcs-esc1 requires adcs).

image_id.description: Use an existing image instead of the marketplace publisher/offer/sku for `os` — e.g. a golden workstation image with an EDR agent pre-installed. Azure: a full resource ID, either a managed image (.../Microsoft.Compute/images/<name>) or a Shared Image Gallery version (.../Microsoft.Compute/galleries/<gallery>/images/<definition>/versions/<version>) — consumed by infra-azure today. AWS: intended to hold an AMI id (ami-xxxxxxxx) once infra-aws exists; not consumed by anything yet. `os` is still required when image_id is set — it still drives which ansible-lockdown role/OS-specific behavior applies, independent of which image backs the VM.

vm_size.description: Cloud VM size for this machine, overriding the per-role default (Azure: e.g. 'Standard_B2s'). Set it here when a role needs a bigger box or the subscription's regional vCPU quota forces a specific SKU (the #1 deploy blocker) — no need to touch templates. When absent, windows.tf's per-role default applies. On a quota-restricted subscription, verify the size exists in the region with the Azure MCP / `az vm list-skus` before deploy.

seed.description: Drives PurpleForge's own deterministic population generator (scripts/population.py) and theming — same seed always produces the same OU tree/users/groups/computers.

include_noise_acls.description: Whether to add BadBlood-style random GenericAll grants (realistic misconfiguration clutter) on top of the deliberately-injected vulnerabilities. Default true (matches prior BadBlood-based behavior); set false for a cleaner signal-to-noise ratio, e.g. when attack_chain.mode is ctf.

role_or_all.description: 'all', or an explicit list of machine roles.

profile.description: Fixes defaults for edr/hardening/deception; entries below are fine-grained overrides on top of the profile.

settings.description: Product-specific settings, e.g. { asr_rules: audit, tamper_protection: true }.

ntlmv2_only.description: Restricts LAN Manager auth to NTLMv2-only, refusing LM/NTLMv1 (LMCompatibilityLevel=5). Verified against ansible-lockdown CIS rule 2.3.11.7 (level1, identical on Windows-2019-CIS/Windows-2022-CIS) — see catalog/defense/hardening/control-cis-rules.yml. Neutralizes catalog/vulnerabilities/ntlm-downgrade.yml.

intentional_gaps_auto.description: If true, the reconciliation step automatically derives skip_rule exclusions from each selected vuln's neutralized_by list.

mode.description: 'independent' (default): every selected vulnerability targets its own real population object, no deliberate overlap. 'ctf': resolve_attack_chain() prefers reusing the same real object across multiple selected vulnerabilities where their target_shape is compatible, so exploiting one is a real prerequisite for the next.
